title: Simple two-team project: normal main chain and AgentRun crash recovery
description: Eval 1 (two teams, no failures, reference trajectory) and Eval 5 (AgentRun checkpoint recovery). All refs are fixture-internal semantic identifiers.

scenarios.summary: Agent worker crashes after checkpoint persistence, before run terminal. A recovery worker claims the run with a new fencing token, stale-token writes are rejected, and the trajectory converges to the same terminal state as Eval 1.

payload.note: submitted by recovery worker worker-B after checkpoint resume

created_or_updated.note: execution_state running->interrupted; crash is a run-level fault: no domain fact, no process transition, task stays in_progress

observations: run-frontend-1 unaffected; RUNNING remains valid via run-frontend-1.
Stale fencing write rejected (G-INV-14); only a security audit row is produced, no durable domain effect.

created_or_updated.note: version=1 exactly one final version despite crash

observations: Recovery worker worker-B claims run-backend-1 with a new lease and fencing token; pre-checkpoint side effects are not repeated.
Recovery audit event records the recovery executor separately; initiated_by/executed_as of run-backend-1 unchanged (G-INV-06).

required_outputs.statement: run-backend-1 resumes from the persisted checkpoint under worker-B with a new fencing token; pre-crash side effects are not repeated.
task-backend-api has exactly one submitted (idem:task-backend-api:submit:v1) and one verified; resource-api-spec has exactly one final version.
A separate recovery audit event exists; initiated_by/executed_as and delegation scope digest of run-backend-1 are unchanged across recovery.
Usage for run-backend-1 counted exactly once under idem:run-backend-1:terminal despite the crash window.
Final state matches eval-01-simple-project: TERMINAL/COMPLETED with delivery-1 ACCEPTED.

forbidden_outcomes.statement: The crash marks run-backend-1 failed-terminal or reverts task-backend-api to accepted/proposed.
The crash fails or cancels the project process.
Any write performed with worker-A's stale fencing token takes effect.
A second parallel run is created for task-backend-api instead of resuming run-backend-1.
Usage double-counted via the recovery replay.
Two submitted versions of resource-api-spec exist.

safety_invariants.statement: Crash window steps t01-t02 produce no domain fact, no transition, and version/sequence deltas of zero.
run-frontend-1 execution and audit are unaffected by the backend crash.

crash_and_recovery.expected_behavior: Run-level crash leaves the process triple unchanged; task stays in_progress; no domain fact.
crash_and_recovery.recovery_signal: Lease expiry allows worker-B to claim run-backend-1 with a new fencing token and resume from checkpoint.
crash_and_recovery.idempotency_requirement: Post-checkpoint side effects not repeated; submit/verify/usage exactly once under stable keys.

crash_and_recovery.expected_behavior: Write with the expired fencing token is rejected.
crash_and_recovery.recovery_signal: Rejection is the expected outcome; only a security audit row remains.
crash_and_recovery.idempotency_requirement: No durable domain effect from the rejected write.
